H06-pos1.label: violation
H06-pos1.note: The controller rejects donations below a business minimum by branching on the amount.

H06-pos2.label: violation
H06-pos2.note: The vendor gateway decides which plays are royalty-bearing by branching on duration and skips the report.

H06-twin1.label: clean
H06-twin1.note: The controller only checks the transport shape of the amount and email.

H06-twin2.label: clean
H06-twin2.note: The same short-play rule lives in a domain policy consulted by the use case.

H06-legit.label: clean
H06-legit.note: The controller maps domain error types to HTTP statuses without deciding anything.

H08-pos1.label: violation
H08-pos1.note: The use case pulls the notifier from a static registry at run time.

H08-pos2.label: violation
H08-pos2.note: The controller obtains the notifier through a helper that calls container.get.

H08-twin1.label: clean
H08-twin1.note: The registry is used only in the composition root; the use case receives the notifier by constructor.

H08-twin2.label: clean
H08-twin2.note: The controller gets a notifier provider function through its constructor.

H08-legit.label: clean
H08-legit.note: The use case receives a map of notifier channels by constructor and reads from that data structure.

H11-pos1.label: violation
H11-pos1.note: A domain string-literal union copies the vendor's status codes.

H11-pos2.label: violation
H11-pos2.note: A port declares an enum whose values copy the vendor's precision codes.

H11-twin1.label: clean
H11-twin1.note: The domain union expresses the same idea in the core's own words.

H11-twin2.label: clean
H11-twin2.note: The domain enum for report granularity uses the core's own values.

H11-legit.label: clean
H11-legit.note: Vendor error codes are used only inside the vendor adapter.
